_comment: Adapter-level DSP/parsing config for MAFAULDA (Machinery Fault Database, UFRJ) — Phase 8. Consumed only by src/vib_agent/adapters/mafaulda.py — never by pdm_core. Not a pdm_core tunable, so it is not subject to the profiles.route whitelist; it configures signal preprocessing and dataset provenance, not detector/gate/confidence logic. Mirrors config/mfpt.json's structure and discipline.
_attribution: MAFAULDA :: Machinery Fault Database [Online], Signals, Multimedia and Telecommunications Laboratory, COPPE/Poli/UFRJ. https://www02.smt.ufrj.br/~offshore/mfs/ — contact Felipe M. L. Ribeiro (felipe.ribeiro@smt.ufrj.br). 1951 multivariate sequences from a SpectraQuest Alignment/Balance Vibration Trainer (ABVT) Machinery Fault Simulator. Held in data/ (gitignored), never redistributed.
_record_note: Official docs section 1.4: 'Each sequence was generated at a 50 kHz sampling rate during 5 s, totaling 250.000 samples.' Asserted at parse time against the actual row count, never assumed silently.
_columns_note: Column order transcribed VERBATIM from the official docs (https://www02.smt.ufrj.br/~offshore/mfs/page_01.html section 2), confirmed at runtime rather than hardcoded blind: 'column 1: tachometer signal that allows to estimate rotation frequency; columns 2 to 4: underhang bearing accelerometer (axial, radial and tangential direction); columns 5 to 7: overhang bearing accelerometer (axial, radial and tangential direction); column 8: microphone.' Files carry NO header row (verified). Microphone is ignored (column 8), per the Phase 8 spec.
_axis_mapping_note: The underhang triax is the primary measurement point (Phase 8 spec). Mapped into MachineMeta axis semantics as: axial -> 'x' (with machine.axial_axis='x'), radial -> 'y', tangential -> 'z'. pdm_core derives radial = the two non-axial axes (bearing_rca.py::_build_context), so ctx.radial becomes ('y','z') = the radial and tangential planes — exactly the two radial planes the spec describes. Overhang channels (columns 5-7) are retained as secondary context only in v1 and are NOT fed to the detectors.
_spectrum_note: RAW acceleration spectrum, NOT an envelope spectrum — a deliberate, load-bearing departure from config/cwru.json and config/mfpt.json, and the single most important design decision in this phase. Those datasets hunt BEARING defect frequencies, which are carried as amplitude MODULATION of a high-frequency resonance, so envelope demodulation is the correct (and necessary) preprocessing. Phase 8 instead validates IMBALANCE and the MISALIGNMENT family, which pdm_core detects from discrete 1x/2x/3x shaft-harmonic LINES (bearing_rca.py::detect_imbalance requires has_1x_radial; detect_misalignment_family keys on 1x/2x across axial vs radial). Those lines are genuine spectral content in a raw spectrum. In an ENVELOPE spectrum, energy at 1x is a demodulation artifact, NOT a velocity-domain imbalance signature — feeding an envelope to these detectors is a category error. Phase 7B demonstrated exactly this failure on real data: MFPT baseline_1 (a healthy rig file, envelope-fed) produced a false 'rotor imbalance, medium confidence' primary finding because its envelope's loudest bin sits at exactly 1.00x shaft. See outputs/wind_turbine_results.md section 6.
_spectrum_region_note: Restricting the raw spectrum to 0-500 Hz is standard practice for 1x/2x analysis and is required here for a specific reason: acceleration amplitude scales with frequency^2 relative to velocity, so an unrestricted 0-25 kHz acceleration spectrum is dominated by high-frequency content and the 1x/2x lines (12-61 Hz shaft => 1x at 12-61 Hz, 2x at 24-123 Hz) would never enter peaks_from_spectrum()'s top-3-per-axis candidate set. 0-500 Hz spans 1x through ~8x at the highest rig speed (61.4 Hz) and through 40x at the lowest (12.3 Hz). Same region bound as config/cwru.json / config/mfpt.json use for their envelope region — reused rather than newly tuned.
_tach_note: Shaft speed comes FROM THE TACHOMETER CHANNEL, not the filename (Phase 8 spec, explicit). The filename does encode a nominal rotation frequency (e.g. normal/12.288.csv = 12.288 Hz) and is used ONLY as the directory-implied cross-check value. The tach is an analog Monarch MT-190 signal (a pulse train, unlike the wind-turbine set's pulse-TIME vector), so the rotation frequency is extracted as the dominant FFT peak of that channel.
_cross_check_note: Spec: 'cross-check against directory-implied speed, flag >2% disagreement'. Flags, never raises — a disagreement is a finding to report, not a crash.
_bearing_note: The rig bearing geometry IS published by the dataset (unlike Phase 7B's wind-turbine SKF 32222 J2, which is unobtainable — see BLOCKED_phase7b_bearing_geometry.md), and our formulas reproduce its published orders to within 0.071%. It is supplied here DELIBERATELY even though Phase 8 fetches no bearing-fault files: withholding it would prevent the bearing detectors from running at all, which would make Part A's 'zero fault findings on all 10 normal files' bar trivially easier to pass by removing a whole detector family from contention. That would be gaming the bar. With the geometry present, any bearing false positive on a normal/imbalance/misalignment file is a real finding and gets reported.
_labels_note: Ground truth comes from directory structure and the official docs ONLY (INVARIANT 2, no fabricated ground truth): normal/ ; imbalance/<weight>g/ ; horizontal-misalignment/<shift>mm/ ; vertical-misalignment/<shift>mm/. The official docs name both misalignment categories PARALLEL ('Horizontal Parallel Misalignment', 'Vertical Parallel Misalignment', sections 1.4.3/1.4.4) — recorded for the variant analysis, but per the spec, assertions are made at FAMILY level only and variant is logged, never expected.
_validation_scope_note: Acceleration units (g) -> ISO zones and severity are OUT of scope, consistent with CWRU/MFPT handling. NOTE (Phase 7B finding): validation_scope is currently honored ONLY by eval/runner.py — nothing in report/ or webapp/ reads it, so a drafted PDF from this data will still print an ISO Zone A verdict derived from a 0.00 mm/s velocity that the quality gate itself flags implausible. See outputs/wind_turbine_results.md section 6. Not fixed here (frozen scope); expected to recur in this phase's Part C artifacts.
